title: A Fully Polynomial Randomized Approximation Scheme for Perfect Matchings in General Graphs
main_claim: There is an FPRAS for the number of perfect matchings of an arbitrary simple graph. Approach: annealing from K_n while suppressing nonedges; vertex scales keep the two-hole ratios balanced. A hole bound (Thm 3.1) plus a path subdivision and tree-bag clique enlargement give inflation at most 2, and marked probe edges expose the partition ratios. Sampling on the tree-bag graph uses a replicated multi-tier product chain. Its spectral gap comes from a two-coordinate pair-energy inequality (Thm 5.1), proved through a label-adapted quadrangulation, a signed cell identity, two-matching encodings and a cycle-swap control of context errors. An ordered ANOVA argument then gives the full spectral gap (Lemma 6.2).

Read and checked Sections 1–8 (main.tex lines 118–3080); skimmed only the corollary section 9 on prescribed degrees. Checks:

- Proof of Thm 3.1: derivative identities, C(n,2)·1e5·n/D0<1e-3, continuity argument, injection of the pairing.

- Probe identity (Prop 4.2).
- Deletion accounting: prefix ratio P(j) and the neutral-pair factors.
- Threshold-charging proof of F·Φ_{B'}(U)≤Φ_B(R), including cross pairs and away-mapped holes.
- Inflation sum 2/99.
- Quadrangulation Lemma 5.1: all cases (a)–(d) and the not-good-exterior case, index parities, conditions (i) and (ii), cell count.
- Cell comparability: distance ≤6, ratio 192D.
- Pair kernel: proposal probabilities; cell identity, including the sign bookkeeping for complementary diagonal gains and cells = diagonals + 1.
- Encodings: added/dropped counts 2+r, the A_0^4 weight bound, inverse via the multiset union, tag count < (10N)^30.
- Conditional demand mass and the Jensen step cancelling p_X; swap-sum (2N identities per cycle).
- Variance-to-cycle decomposition via the involution toggling earlier cycles; final constant arithmetic.
- Replica gap: unequal-tier comparison via Metropolis capacity, martingale decomposition, ANOVA residual uniqueness (y last, x penultimate), absorption with q=32L, refresh energy.
- Tier density ratio, minimum mass Λ, mixing bound.
- Counting stage: balance propagation (1/16 lower bound, 512α), estimator error bounds, Hoeffding/union bound, padding bias, median amplification, bit-length accounting for the scales.
sibling_notes: There were no prior sibling entries for family 113 on the board. I posted a no_gap_found summary. Note for siblings: the load-bearing novel step is Thm 5.1 (pair energy inequality via quadrangulation, cell identity and cycle-swap control of context errors) combined with Lemma 6.2 (ANOVA replica gap). I re-derived both line by line and found no failing step, but given the significance of the claim (an open problem since Jerrum–Sinclair 1989), they warrant independent expert review. The constants (L=(10^4ND)^100, q=32L) are polynomial but astronomically large.
